summary: August Winter was an Indologist. He studied under Hermann Jacobi at the University of Bonn (~1889–1892) and completed his Ph.D. under Alfred Hillebrandt at the University of Breslau (~1892–1893).

August Zacharias Collin worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned his fil.kand. and fil.dr. at Lund University and studied under Rudolf von Roth (1874–1875). He was Docent of chemistry at Lund (1858) and Lektor at Nicolaiskolan, Helsingborg (1864).

Auguste Ali Bourquin worked in Indology and religious studies. He earned a Dr.théol. from the University of Paris by 1885, served with the Scottish Mission at Wilson College, Mumbai (1882), and held a post at the Royal College of Science, Arts and Commerce.

Auguste Barth was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied under Frédéric-Guillaume Bergmann at the University of Strasbourg (~1853–1856), taught at Collège de Bouxwiller and Collège Poincaré Saverne, co-founded the EFEO, and joined the Institut de France.
Auguste Comte was a philosopher. He studied at the Lycée Joffre until 1814 and then at the École polytechnique from 1814 to 1816.

Auguste Desgodins was a Tibetologist and linguist. He studied at the Major Seminary of Verdun (~1845–1848) and the Séminaire de Saint-Sulpice (~1848–1850), later serving as a missionary with the Paris Foreign Missions Society from 1855.

Auguste Wagener worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Bonn under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl and Christian Lassen (1845–1849) and at the University of Liège (~1846–1850). He held posts at Ghent University as agrégé (1850) and professor (1858).

Auguste-Louis-Armand Loiseleur-Deslongchamps was an Indologist. He was educated at Lycée Charlemagne and studied under Antoine-Léonard Chézy and Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy in 1824. In 1832, he joined the Manuscript Department of the Bibliothèque nationale de France.

Augustus Frederic Rudolf Hoernle worked in Indology and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Basel, under Theodor Goldstücker (1860), and at Tübingen. He held posts at Jay Narayan Inter College, Cathedral Mission College, Calcutta Madrasa/Aliah University, and The Asiatic Society.

Aung San Suu Kyi is active in Tibetology and other fields. She studied at Basic Education High School No. 1 Dagon, Lady Shri Ram College, Delhi University, St Hugh's College, and SOAS, and worked at the United Nations (~1969–1971).

Aurel Mayr was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University, Vienna, Berlin under Albrecht Weber, and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth (Ph.D. 1870–1871). He was professor of Sanskrit and IE linguistics at Eötvös Loránd University (1873–1905).
Aureliano Julio Berriz do Seixo was an Indologist. He earned a doctorate in Civil and Canonic Law from the Complutense University of Madrid, where he later served as Assistant Professor of Sanskrit.

Awadh Kishore Narain was an Indologist, archaeologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at BHU and SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham, he held multiple chairs, directorships, and deanships at BHU and served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1971–1987).

Axel Erdmann was a linguist and Indologist. He earned his fil.kand. and fil.dr. at Uppsala University and studied under Johann Gildemeister at the University of Bonn (1872–1873). He spent his academic career at Uppsala University, becoming Professor of English in 1904.

Axel Klein specializes in Japanology and other fields. He studied at the University of Bonn (1987–1994), worked there and at the German Institute for Japanese Studies, and became a professor of modern East Asian studies at the University of Duisburg-Essen in 2012.

Axel Michaels is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Hamburg and Kiel, learning under Albrecht Wezler and Laxmi Nath Srestha. His main posts include director at the Nepal Research Centre and Heidelberg University, and professor at Bern and Kiel.
Ayako Nakamura works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned a PhD from the University of Hamburg (attested 2009), where she also held a post as a Research Fellow (attested 2026).

Ayinapalli Aiyappan worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Madras (~1925–1927). He served as Superintendent at the Government Museum, Chennai (~1940–1960), and held a post at the University of Kerala (~1968–1969).

Ayu Khandro was a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Drodul Pawo Dorje, Nyala Pema Dündul, and Chokgyur Lingpa, and taught A Dzom Gyalsé Gyurmé Dorjé and Namkhai Norbu.
Ayush Maheshwari works in computational fields and Indology. He earned his PhD and holds a post at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay.
